quick.summary: How to make sure different teams report the same numbers without causing chaos.
quick.takeaway: Define one shared list for shared data. Let local teams keep their own views.

beats.line: Three teams gave me sales totals. None of them match. Why does this happen?
Because they all count differently. Think of a road sign.
If every town picked its own stop sign color, driving would be chaos.
So we need one rule for everyone.
Exactly. We call it canonical reference data.
Can I just say one shared list?
Yes. Pick one list of regions.
And force everyone to use it?
Just the systems that share data. Local teams can keep their own views.
So I publish the official list and check that central reports use it.
That is how you stop the chaos.

quiz.question: What is the best way to handle reference data across a large company?
options: Force every single team to change their internal tables.
Create one shared list for systems that talk to each other.
Let every team decide how to label their own shared data.
Build a translation tool for every pair of teams.
quiz.explanation: You only need a standard for data that moves between systems. Local teams can keep local views.

quiz.question: Setting a data standard means picking one rule and applying it to shared systems.
quiz.explanation: True. Standards act like road signs. They only work if everyone driving on the shared road follows them.
